newsitem.title: INDIA: India moving towards rupee convertibility - Finmin. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India moving towards rupee convertibility - Finmin. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]

text.p: India has for the first time met some of the conditions needed to make the rupee convertible on capital (corrects from current) account, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday.

"I think for the first time we are confident we can meet some of the pre-conditions," Chidambaram told state-run Doordarshan television after presenting the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament.
He was referring to guidelines set by the central bank, including adequate foreign exchange reserves, low inflation and high exports.
"I don't think two, three years ago we were in a position to meet these pre-conditions," Chidambaram said. "On the capital account convertibility, I don't think the step has come too late."
Earlier, in his budget speech to parliament, Chidambaram said the time had come for "preparatory work" towards capital account convertibility.
Chidambaram said the government was asking the Reserve Bank of India to set up a panel of experts to pave the way towards making the rupee convertible on capital account.
The rupee can currently be converted freely for transactions in goods and services but the government exercises control over capital transactions.
